items.followUp: What is the purpose of the `alt` attribute in an HTML image tag?

rubric.why: Identifies that the attribute adds a border to the image.
rubric.description: States that the border attribute adds a border around an image.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its border function.

rubric.why: Explains that the border’s width or thickness can be specified.
rubric.description: Mentions that the border’s thickness or width can be set.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the border’s size setting.

modelAnswer: The `border` attribute is used to display a border around an image.
Its value specifies the border’s thickness, usually in pixels.

items.followUp: Give two reasons why a website may use encryption.

rubric.why: Names the person or device that sends information.
rubric.description: Identifies the sender/source as a component of a communication system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the sender or source.

rubric.why: Names the person or device that receives information.
rubric.description: Identifies the receiver/destination as a component of a communication system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the receiver or destination.

rubric.description: Identifies the message/data as a component of a communication system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the message or data.

rubric.why: Names the path through which information travels.
rubric.description: Identifies the communication medium/channel as a component of a communication system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the medium or channel.

modelAnswer: Sender: the person or device that sends the information.
Message: the information or data being communicated.
Communication medium: the path through which the information travels.
Receiver: the person or device that receives the information.

items.followUp: Explain two ways encryption helps protect an online banking account.

rubric.why: Recognizes that encryption keeps information private.
rubric.description: Explains that encryption keeps personal information confidential.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it protects privacy or confidentiality.

rubric.why: Recognizes that encryption makes information harder for unauthorized people to access.
rubric.description: Explains that encryption helps prevent unauthorized access to data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning protection from unauthorized access.

rubric.why: Gives a relevant everyday Internet use.
rubric.description: Connects encryption with securing online banking or transactions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant example such as online banking or transactions.

rubric.why: Identifies sensitive information that encryption helps protect.
rubric.description: Mentions protection of passwords, login credentials or personal data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming sensitive information protected by encryption.

modelAnswer: Encryption converts readable information into coded form so that others cannot easily understand it.
It protects private information, such as passwords and personal data, when it is sent over the Internet.
It helps prevent unauthorized people from accessing or misusing this information.
It is important for secure everyday activities such as online banking and other Internet transactions.

items.followUp: Describe how the divide and conquer rule can be used to solve a large problem.

rubric.why: States the problem is split into smaller parts.
rubric.description: Explains that a large problem is divided into smaller subproblems.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the division into smaller parts.

rubric.why: States that the smaller parts are solved and their results brought together.
rubric.description: Explains that subproblems are solved and their solutions combined.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing solving and combining the subproblem results.

modelAnswer: The divide and conquer rule breaks a large problem into smaller subproblems.
The subproblems are solved separately, and their solutions are combined to solve the original problem.
